method: Agent-enumerated from domain knowledge of EU OJ publications, FATF plenary outputs, UNSC resolutions, G7/G20 communiqués, and OECD CARF publications. Cross-checked against events/*.yaml and candidate_triggers/*.yaml at generation time. No automated scraper used.
cross_check_method: Each candidate slug verified absent from events/ and candidate_triggers/ before inclusion. Existing S6 events are eu-mica-2023, eu-russia-crypto-wallet-cap-2022 (5th package), eu-russia-full-crypto-wallet-ban-2022 (8th package), eu-12th-russia-sanctions-2023. Korea Travel Rule (korea-travel-rule-2022) is jurisdictional (KR) S4 not S6 — only the global FATF parent guidance is enumerated here.
exclusion_notes: EU 1st-4th Russia sanctions packages (2014-2015) excluded — pre-2017 scope window and pre-crypto-explicit (no crypto-asset clauses in 833/2014 until 5th package 2022-04).

EU 6th and 7th Russia packages (2022-06, 2022-07) excluded — they did not add new crypto-specific provisions on top of the 5th-package Article 5b; the 8th package is the structural crypto pivot (already covered as eu-russia-full-crypto-wallet-ban-2022).

EU 9th, 10th, 11th Russia packages (Dec 2022 / Feb 2023 / Jun 2023) excluded as P3 — they extend non-crypto restrictions and tweak Article 5aa wording without a crypto-services pivot comparable to 5th/8th/12th. Verify-before-admit if needed; not enumerated here.

EU 13th, 14th, 15th Russia packages (Feb 2024 / Jun 2024 / Dec 2024) enumerated below where they materially expanded crypto-services provisions; the 14th-package 2024-06 SPFS/financial-messaging extension is the cleanest crypto-adjacent pivot among them and is enumerated as P1.
EU Iran sanctions: existing EU restrictive measures against Iran (Regulation 267/2012 + amendments) do not contain explicit crypto-services clauses through 2025-12; excluded.

EU Belarus sanctions: crypto-services provisions added by Regulation 765/2006 amendments (2022-2023) closely mirror the Russia clauses and are derivative — only the lead Belarus crypto-services event is enumerated (P2).
UN DPRK Panel of Experts annual reports — these are reporting documents (S/2019/171, S/2020/151, etc.), not censorship triggers. Not enumerated; the 2017 UNSC sanctions are the trigger axis.
Council of Europe — no crypto-specific convention exists through 2025-12; excluded.
WTO — no crypto-services regime statements with censorship effect; excluded.
G7 statements on crypto (Hiroshima 2023, Apulia 2024) are endorsements without binding effect — included only as P2 collective-action anchors with thin observable cascade.

MiCA secondary legislation: ESMA / EBA / ESAs Regulatory Technical Standards (RTS) and Implementing Technical Standards (ITS) published in batches 2024-Q1 through 2024-Q4. The single most consequential RTS package (Jul-Dec 2024 batch) is enumerated as P1; per-RTS atomization deferred to P3 verify-if-needed.

candidates.target: Global VASP ecosystem — first FATF guidance applying Recommendation 16 (Travel Rule) to virtual-asset transfers and Recommendation 15 to VASP licensing/registration
candidates.one_line_rationale: Foundational supranational trigger that downstream every national Travel Rule (KR 2022, JP 2023, EU MiCA 2023, US BSA proposals, UK MLR 2022) cites; the 2019-06 plenary guidance reset the global compliance baseline. Conspicuously absent — korea-travel-rule-2022 references FATF R.16 but no parent FATF event is in the corpus.

candidates.target: Global VASP ecosystem — updated guidance covering stablecoins, DeFi, NFTs, peer-to-peer transactions, P2P unhosted-wallet treatment
candidates.one_line_rationale: First FATF guidance to extend Recommendation 15 scope to DeFi developers ("control or sufficient influence over" test) and to stablecoin issuers; trigger for the 2022-2024 VASP-licensing pressure cascade that pushed Tornado-Cash-style protocols toward regulatory scope. Cited by EU MiCA recitals.

candidates.target: Global VASP ecosystem — 2023 Targeted Update reporting that only 35/151 jurisdictions had Travel Rule legislation; named-and-shamed compliance laggards
candidates.one_line_rationale: First public FATF country-level compliance scorecard for crypto; the named-laggard pressure directly preceded the 2024 implementation wave (CARF, EU MiCA L2). Important for documenting peer-pressure cascade in S6.

candidates.target: Global crypto-asset reporting ecosystem — OECD CARF technical standard for automatic exchange of tax information on crypto-asset transactions
candidates.one_line_rationale: G20-endorsed tax-transparency framework requiring CASPs to report user-level transaction data to tax authorities for automatic exchange. First binding supranational reporting standard for crypto; downstream of CRS (2014). EU adopted as DAC8 directive 2023-10. Foundational S6 anchor.

candidates.target: EU CASP ecosystem — Council Directive (EU) 2023/2226 (DAC8) requiring CASP reporting of user transactions to EU tax authorities
candidates.one_line_rationale: EU implementation of OECD CARF as Directive 2023/2226; applies from 2026-01-01. Pairs with eu-mica-2023 as the tax-reporting axis of the EU crypto framework. The MiCA event covers licensing; DAC8 covers reporting; both are necessary for the S6 EU baseline.

candidates.target: EU CASP ecosystem — Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 (TFR recast) extending FATF Travel Rule to crypto transfers; no de-minimis threshold
candidates.one_line_rationale: EU-level Travel Rule implementation companion to MiCA, adopted same legislative package; mandates originator/beneficiary info for every crypto transfer from EU CASPs (no threshold). Applies from 2024-12-30. Cleanest supranational Travel Rule implementation in the dataset; KR/JP precede it but EU is the first multi-state binding implementation.

candidates.target: EU AML/CFT supervisory ecosystem — Regulation (EU) 2024/1620 establishing the Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) with direct supervision over high-risk CASPs
candidates.one_line_rationale: First EU-level AML supervisor with direct (non-NCA-mediated) jurisdiction over CASPs above thresholds. Frankfurt-seated AMLA begins operations 2025-07 and assumes direct supervision 2028. Structurally distinct from MiCA (CASP licensing) — AMLA covers AML/CFT compliance enforcement. Critical baseline event.

candidates.target: EU AML/CFT ecosystem — Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR) single rulebook including CASP-specific provisions (CDD, beneficial ownership, self-hosted-wallet caps)
candidates.one_line_rationale: Companion to AMLA Regulation 2024/1620; sets EUR 1,000 threshold for CASP CDD on self-hosted-wallet transfers and EUR 10,000 anonymous-payment cap. First binding supranational rules on unhosted-wallet treatment in the corpus. Applies from 2027-07-10.

candidates.target: DPRK state and DPRK-affiliated actors (precursor framing — does not name crypto explicitly but UN 1718 Panel of Experts subsequently treats crypto-asset theft as 1718-sanctioned activity)
candidates.one_line_rationale: UNSC Resolution 2371 (2017) — DPRK sanctions tightening; first resolution era in which the UN 1718 Panel of Experts begins documenting DPRK-state crypto theft (Lazarus Group). Not crypto-explicit but is the legal substrate cited by US OFAC Lazarus designations and by national CASP DPRK-screening compliance. P1 because not crypto-explicit in text.

candidates.target: G20 member-state crypto regulatory ecosystems — joint IMF-FSB synthesis paper and G20 New Delhi Leaders Declaration endorsing crypto-asset policy framework
candidates.one_line_rationale: Cleanest G20 collective-action anchor on crypto in the 2017-2025 window; endorses FSB high-level recommendations + IMF capital-flow guidance + FATF Travel Rule + OECD CARF. Predates EU DAC8 and MiCA L2 — sets the political ceiling for national implementations. Observable cascade is policy-coordination not direct-action; P1 for that reason.

candidates.target: Global crypto-asset and stablecoin issuer ecosystems — FSB high-level recommendations for crypto-asset and stablecoin regulation (CA-R and SC-R)
candidates.one_line_rationale: Financial Stability Board's first finalized recommendations on crypto-assets and global stablecoins; endorsed by G20 same year. Directly cited by EU MiCA implementation and by UK FCA stablecoin rulemaking 2024. Slot under S6 because FSB is treaty-supranational (G20 mandate). Verify whether FSB actor enum exists or needs addition.

candidates.target: Russian shadow-fleet operators + sanctions-circumvention CASPs — Council Regulation (EU) 2024/3192; expands designation track for crypto-circumvention facilitators
candidates.one_line_rationale: 15th package: first EU sanctions package to add named crypto-circumvention facilitators (similar to Garantex pattern) under the Russia regime — supranational analogue to the OFAC Garantex/Aeza track. Distinct from the 12th-package class prohibition (already in corpus).

candidates.target: Russian SPFS financial-messaging network + non-EU CASPs facilitating SPFS — Council Regulation (EU) 2024/1739 extends Russia sanctions to non-EU SPFS-using entities
candidates.one_line_rationale: 14th package: extraterritorial expansion of EU sanctions to non-EU entities using Russia's SPFS payment system; cited by EU CASPs as basis for offboarding third-country counterparts. Crypto-adjacent: explicit financial-messaging-network restriction with crypto-rail implications.

candidates.target: Belarus-resident natural and legal persons — Council Regulation (EU) 2022/398 amending Regulation 765/2006 to prohibit EU operators providing crypto-asset wallets/accounts/custody services above EUR 10,000
candidates.one_line_rationale: Belarus-regime analogue to the Russia 5th-package crypto cap (eu-russia-crypto-wallet-cap-2022). P2 because derivative-mirror of the Russia regime; admit only if dataset rewards Belarus-regime granularity beyond the Russia parent.

candidates.target: EU CASP ecosystem — ESMA + EBA + EIOPA bundled Regulatory Technical Standards (RTS) and Implementing Technical Standards (ITS) under MiCA Title II/III/IV/V
candidates.one_line_rationale: MiCA secondary legislation bundle published 2024-07 through 2024-12; operationalizes MiCA Level-1. Includes ART/EMT recovery & redemption plans, CASP authorization templates, ICT risk management requirements. Slot at the bundle level (single triage entry) to avoid 12-13 per-RTS atomization; can be split later if needed.

candidates.target: FATF grey-listed jurisdictions citing crypto-asset deficiencies — South Africa, UAE (later removed), Nigeria, Bulgaria — public statement at the Oct-2023 plenary
candidates.one_line_rationale: First FATF plenary statements naming crypto-asset AML deficiencies as a load-bearing reason for grey-list inclusion (South Africa) and removal-blocker (UAE). P2 because the grey-list cascade is mediated through national CASP-derisking actions rather than direct supranational mandate; the parent FATF guidance events carry the load-bearing observation.

candidates.target: G7 member-state crypto regulatory ecosystems — Hiroshima Leaders' Communiqué endorsing FATF Travel Rule full implementation and crypto-asset cross-border supervision
candidates.one_line_rationale: G7 collective endorsement; observable cascade thin (no direct binding effect — G7 communiqués are political commitments). P2 unless dataset benefits from policy-coordination markers separate from G20-roadmap-crypto-asset-policy-2023.
